content.title: Scope of Application and Definition of Subject Persons (Statutory Jurisdiction)
content.conditions: The provisions of this law apply to all active-duty officers and personnel of the Internal Security Forces, as well as students of the Police College, institutes, and specialized training academies. It further extends to retired, dismissed, discharged, and resigned personnel if the offense was committed during and arising out of the performance of official duty, irrespective of any subsequent alteration in their administrative status.
content.penalties: Subjection of offenders to prosecution before the Internal Security Forces Courts and the uniform enforcement of statutory penalties across all designated categories without prejudice, ensuring the recovery of public and private rights accrued to the Ministry or victims.

content.title: Classification and Types of Statutory Penalties
content.conditions: Penalties applicable to the Internal Security Forces are categorized into three primary classes: Principal Penalties (Death Penalty, Life Imprisonment, Temporary Imprisonment, Detention, Dismissal from Service), Accessory and Supplementary Penalties (Deprivation of rights and privileges, forfeiture of medals and decorations), and Disciplinary and Administrative Penalties (Reprimand, salary deduction, room confinement, unit confinement, extra duties, extra training).

content.title: Felony of High Treason and Collaboration with the Enemy or Terrorist Organizations
content.conditions: Any officer or personnel who willfully aids the enemy or designated terrorist entities, divulges classified security intelligence and tactical defense plans of the Internal Security Forces, surrenders state-owned weaponry, munitions, or military assets to the enemy, or deserts post and flees during active combat or hostile engagement.
content.penalties: Imposition of the Death Penalty or Life Imprisonment, mandatory summary dismissal from military and security service, and total statutory forfeiture of all accrued financial rights and pension entitlements.

content.title: Felony of Mutiny and Armed Insurrection within Security Forces
content.conditions: The conspiracy or concerted assembly of two or more officers or personnel of the Security and Police Forces with the intent to mutiny against lawful command authority, or the deployment of armed force and violence to seize security headquarters or obstruct the execution of statutory duties during states of emergency or normal operations.
content.penalties: Imposition of the Death Penalty upon ringleaders and instigators of the mutiny, and Temporary Imprisonment (ranging from 5 to 15 years) for subordinate participants, accompanied by summary dismissal from service and forfeiture of pension entitlements.

content.title: Felony of Incitement to Mutiny and Subversion of Discipline
content.conditions: Any personnel or officer who disseminates propaganda or incites mutiny or disobedience to superior orders, or circulates false rumors and misleading reports within the ranks of the Internal Security Forces with the intent to demoralize personnel and undermine military and security discipline.
content.penalties: Imposition of Temporary Imprisonment for a term not exceeding 10 years during peacetime operations, subject to statutory escalation to Life Imprisonment or the Death Penalty if committed during wartime or active counter-terrorism operations.

content.title: Principle of Legality of Crimes and Punishments (Nullum crimen, nulla poena sine lege)
content.conditions: No act or omission shall constitute a criminal offense or be subject to punishment except by virtue of an explicit statutory provision in force at the time of its commission. Furthermore, no penalty or precautionary measure may be imposed unless expressly prescribed by law.
content.penalties: Application of the statutory doctrine prohibiting retroactive or extra-statutory criminalization, whereby courts lack jurisdiction to impose unprescribed sanctions, mandating the dismissal of charges based on non-statutory acts and declaring the acquittal of the accused.

content.title: Temporal Jurisdiction of Penal Law and Application of the Law Most Favorable to the Accused (Lex Mitior)
content.conditions: A criminal offense is governed by the statute in force at the time of its commission, determined by the time the operative act was committed irrespective of when its consequence occurred. However, if one or more statutes are enacted after the commission of the offense and prior to the judgment becoming final and conclusive, the statute most favorable to the accused shall apply exclusively.
content.penalties: If the subsequent enactment decriminalizes the act, the execution of the final sentence is immediately stayed and all associated penal consequences are extinguished. If the subsequent enactment merely reduces the statutory penalty, the court retains jurisdiction to review and reduce the sentence upon application by the convicted person or the Public Prosecution.

content.title: Enforcement of Temporary Statutes
content.conditions: If a statute enacted to criminalize an act or aggravate its punishment is limited to a specific duration or temporary emergency circumstance (such as wartime, state of emergency, or economic distress), the expiration of such period or cessation of the circumstance does not preclude the initiation of criminal prosecution or the execution of sentences imposed for offenses committed during its period of validity.
content.penalties: Continued statutory accountability and enforcement of penal sanctions under the temporary statute despite its expiration, preventing offenders from evading legal accountability through the passage of time or the termination of emergency states.

content.title: Territorial Jurisdiction of Penal Law (Principle of Territoriality)
content.conditions: The provisions of this law apply to all offenses committed within the territorial boundaries of the Republic of Iraq. An offense is deemed committed within Iraq if any operative act constituting the offense is executed therein or if its criminal consequence occurs within Iraq, regardless of the offender's nationality whether Iraqi or foreign.
content.penalties: Subjection of the offender to prosecution before Iraqi courts and the enforcement of statutory principal and accessory penalties, subject to recognized exceptions established under international conventions and diplomatic immunities.

content.title: Jurisdiction over Vessels and Aircraft (Flag State and Territorial Waters)
content.conditions: The provisions of this law apply to offenses committed aboard vessels and aircraft flying the Iraqi flag wherever located worldwide. It further applies to offenses committed aboard foreign vessels and aircraft situated within Iraqi airspace or territorial waters if the offense compromises state security or if either the offender or victim is a Republic of Iraq national.

content.title: Functions and Objectives of the Ministry
content.conditions:
The Ministry undertakes the following duties and responsibilities:
First: Protecting, guarding, and defending the Kurdistan Region and ensuring its national and supreme interests.
Second: Protecting the political entity of the Region and its democratic governing system, and preserving its constitutional institutions.
Third: Supporting the Federal Government in defending the sovereignty and security of Iraq pursuant to the Federal Constitution and the Regional Constitution, coordinating and cooperating with it in confronting security crises and disasters, and participating when necessary in war and combating terrorism in all its forms in coordination with the Federal Government.
Fourth: Establishing regular military formations and units and training them in all arts of combat and modern military sciences to qualify them for defending the Region.
Fifth: Formulating necessary plans for the development and modernization of Peshmerga forces, procuring all types of weapons, technical gear, equipment, and developing operational battlefield arts.
Sixth: Providing all matters relating to billeting, armaments, supplies, transportation, rations, salaries, financial and accounting affairs, healthcare, physical fitness, and general services for the forces.

content.title: Organizational Formations of the Ministry of Peshmerga
content.conditions:
The Ministry consists of the following formations:
First: The Minister: The supreme head of the Ministry and the primary official responsible for steering its policies, directing operations, and overseeing its overall activities.
Second: The Deputy Minister: Assists the Minister in managing the Ministry's affairs and exercises the powers delegated under internal bylaws or ministerial assignment.
Third: The Secretary General: Headed by a Secretary General with Special Grade rank, answerable to the Minister, supervising multiple general directorates including: General Directorate of Contracts, Procurement and Armaments; General Directorate of Personnel and Volunteers; General Directorate of Media, Morale Guidance and National Culture; General Directorate of Peshmerga Pension Affairs and Special Needs Care; General Directorate of Budget and Programs (Military Accounting); and the Legal Department and Military Courts.
Fourth: The Inspectorate General: Headed by a senior military officer, tasked with inspection and performance oversight of all formations, units, and facilities of the Ministry.
Fifth: Financial Audit Department: Undertakes financial oversight, audit of accounts, and compliance with statutory financial regulations.
Sixth: Directorate of Coordination and Relations: Regulates relations with relevant civilian and military governmental authorities.
Seventh: The Presidency of the General Staff: Headed by a Staff Officer with deputy chiefs for Operations and Administration/Logistics; comprising directorates of Operations, Planning and Modernization, Military Training, Signals and Communications, Organization, Combat Arms, Logistics and Quartermaster, Military Medical Services, Central Depots, Military Works, and Garrisons.
Eighth: Formations of the Regional Guard (Zeravani): Regulated by a special government regulation.
Ninth: General Directorate of Intelligence: Tasked with military intelligence collection, tactical and strategic security, and facility defense.
Tenth: Reserve Forces Command: Regulated by bylaw.
Eleventh: Ministry Defense Council: Composed of: The Minister (Chairman), Deputy Minister, Secretary General, Chief of Staff, Director General of Military Intelligence, Inspector General, and Commander of the Reserve Forces.

content.title: Definition of Disabled Peshmerga
content.conditions: A Disabled Peshmerga (Regional Guard) is defined as any member who, during the performance of duty or as a consequence thereof, sustains a permanent disability that impedes the continued performance of service.
content.formattedText: Article 1 > Definition of Disabled Peshmerga > A Disabled Peshmerga (Regional Guard) is defined as any member who, during the performance of duty or as a consequence thereof, sustains a permanent disability that impedes the continued performance of service.

content.title: Conditions for Referral to Disability Retirement
content.conditions:
A Peshmerga with permanent disability shall be referred to retirement in the following two circumstances:
First: If the degree of disability reaches fifty percent (50%) or above pursuant to a medical report issued by a competent military medical board.
Second: If the member loses an external bodily limb or organ (organically or functionally), regardless of the overall percentage of disability.

content.title: Disability Pension, Battlefield Promotion, and Bonus
content.conditions:
First: The disabled Peshmerga shall be granted a pension equal to the full last active salary and allowances received during active service, plus disability allowance commensurate with the certified disability rate.
Second: A Peshmerga who sustained disability in the field of battle at a rate of 50% or above shall be granted one higher rank, and his pension shall be computed on the basis of the new rank with honors bonuses.
Third: A Peshmerga sustaining 100% total disability in the field of battle shall be granted two higher ranks, and his pension and allowances shall be calculated according to the upgraded rank.
Fourth: A one-time lump-sum gratuity equal to the total salary received over the final eighteen (18) months shall be disbursed.
Fifth: A disabled Peshmerga who lost an external bodily organ under Article 2(Second) shall receive a limb-loss disability allowance of 50% of total salary.

content.title: Disability Between 25% and 49%
content.conditions: A disabled Peshmerga whose disability percentage ranges between 25% and 49% shall be reassigned to stationary units, or may elect upon personal application to be retired under the provisions of the Peshmerga Service and Retirement Law.

content.title: Designation as Martyr Upon Decease
content.conditions:
A disabled Peshmerga covered by this Law shall be designated as a Martyr upon death in the following manner:
First: If disability resulted from battlefield combat, the file shall be transferred to the Ministry of Martyrs and Anfal Affairs, and full salaries, allowances, and organ-loss stipends shall continue to be paid to the surviving dependents as received prior to death.
Second: If disability occurred during or due to service, the file shall be transferred to the Ministry of Martyrs and Anfal Affairs, and full salaries and allowances received prior to death shall be paid to surviving dependents.

content.title: Living Amenities, Caretaker Allowance, and Medical Care
content.conditions:
First: Competent institutions must provide living necessities and comfort accommodations suited to the disability of the Peshmerga.
Second: A personal attendant/caretaker shall be assigned for a Peshmerga with 100% full disability in cases of: complete paralysis, bilateral amputation above the knee, loss of both hands, complete blindness in both eyes, or post-injury schizophrenia/severe psychosis.
Third: The Kurdistan Regional Government shall bear full responsibility for medical treatment, prosthetics, and physical/social rehabilitation.
Fourth: The disability pension shall automatically be increased by any general increase applied to active serving personnel according to rank and grade.

Fifth: Government commitment to allocate and secure suitable residential housing.

content.title: Legal Definitions
content.conditions:
The following terms and expressions shall have the meanings assigned to them:
1. The Region: The Kurdistan Region - Iraq.
2. Commander-in-Chief: Commander-in-Chief of Peshmerga Forces - Regional Guard.
3. Regional Government: The Kurdistan Regional Government.
4. General Command: The supreme authority of the armed formations of Kurdistan.
5. Peshmerga Forces: All armed components of the Kurdistan Regional Guard from private to general.
6. The Ministry: The Ministry of Peshmerga.
7. The Minister: The Minister of Peshmerga.
8. The Revolution: The stage of the Kurdistan Liberation Movement commencing September 11, 1961.
9. Peshmerga: Anyone who participated in the liberation revolution or enlisted in the Peshmerga forces.
10. Retiree: A Peshmerga entitled to statutory pension rights.
11. Pension: Monthly annuity disbursed upon retirement.
12. Salary: Final monthly base salary received according to rank and post.
13. Full Salary: Base salary plus statutory allowances.
14. Pension Rights: Statutory rights due to the retiree or heirs.
15. Pensionable Service: Creditable revolutionary, active, or authorized added service.
16. Peshmerga Service: Actual active service in the revolution or within Peshmerga formations.
17. Successor: Legal heir under personal status laws.
18. Beneficiary: Eligible dependent entitled to pension after decedent's demise.
19. Missing Person: A Peshmerga missing in action whose fate is unconfirmed.
20. Prisoner of War (POW): Captured by a hostile force during or due to duty.
21. Detainee: Captured or held hostage by an external or terrorist entity due to service.

content.title: Appointment, Promotion, and Retirement of Officers
content.conditions:
First: Commissioning, resignation acceptance, retirement, and recall of officers from the rank of Lieutenant upwards shall be enacted upon the proposal of the Minister with the approval of the Commander-in-Chief.
Second: The Chief of Staff, deputies, division commanders, and special military command posts shall be appointed upon proposal of the General Command and approval of the Commander-in-Chief.

content.title: Conditions for Commissioning as Lieutenant
content.conditions:
The qualifications for commissioning as Lieutenant in the Peshmerga forces are:
1. Must be a citizen of the Kurdistan Region.
2. Aged between 20 and 26 years.
3. Possessing good conduct and reputation, free from felony convictions or dishonorable misdemeanors.
4. Graduate of a recognized military college or 4-year higher education institution/university, or special Peshmerga command courses.
5. Physically fit and medically sound.
6. Age and degree requirements (2 & 4) do not apply to officers awarded ranks in honor of active revolutionary struggle.
7. Graduates of medical and engineering faculties shall be commissioned as First Lieutenants upon voluntary enlistment.

content.title: Volunteer Peshmerga Enlistment
content.conditions:
First: A Volunteer Peshmerga is an enlisted volunteer serving from Private up to Chief Warrant Officer for a designated term.
Second: Enlistment, promotions, branch transfers, terminations, and retirements are executed pursuant to ministerial orders under regulations.

content.title: Volunteer Enlistment Requirements
content.conditions:
Volunteer enlistment conditions require:
1. Regional citizenship.
2. Minimum age of 18.
3. Maximum age of 25 for technical corps and 30 for other branches.
4. Good moral conduct, without felony or dishonorable misdemeanor convictions.
5. Successful completion of sixth primary/basic grade.

content.conditions:

content.title: Crediting Revolutionary and Combat Service
content.conditions:
First: Service in the liberation movement or Peshmerga ranks prior to this Law counts as active service for all pension, increment, seniority, and leave purposes upon verification.
Second: Pre-March 5, 1991 service and designated active combat operational deployments count double (2x) for pension purposes.

content.title: Transfer to Civil Service and Service Portability
content.conditions: If a Peshmerga is appointed or transferred to a civil service post, all Peshmerga service years shall be credited to the new post for all civil service and retirement purposes.

content.title: Contract Officers for Specialized Expertise
content.conditions:
First: The Minister may, with Commander-in-Chief approval, contract professionals as commissioned officers based on specialized technical requirements.
Second: Military rank for contract officers is granted upon ministerial proposal and presidential approval.
content.formattedText:

content.title: Contract Term and Renewals
content.conditions:
First: Initial officer contract term is 10 years, renewable for 3-year increments upon ministerial approval.
Second: The officer is discharged upon contract expiration.
Third: In wartime and state of emergency, contracts may be compulsorily extended.

content.formattedText: Article 14 > Contract Cancellation for Misconduct > The Commander-in-Chief may terminate a contract officer upon recommendation of an investigative board for failure to maintain Peshmerga discipline and ethics.

content.title: Secondment of Personnel
content.conditions:
First: Commissioned officers may be seconded outside Peshmerga formations for up to 3 years, renewable once.
Second: Enlisted volunteers may be seconded for up to 3 years, renewable once.
Third: Seconded personnel return to organic Peshmerga duty upon completion of term.

content.title: Rights and Status During Secondment
content.conditions:
First: Secondment period counts as active military service qualifying for statutory promotions.
Second: Salaries and allowances are defrayed by the host receiving institution.

content.title: Referral to Half-Pay Status
content.conditions:
The Minister may place an officer on half-pay list temporarily due to:
1. Misconduct reported through chain of command.
2. Professional incompetence and failure to perform duties.
3. Academic or operational failure in mandatory branch courses.

2. Established operational incompetence.

content.title: Voluntary Retirement and Severance Below 15 Years
content.conditions:
First: A Peshmerga with at least 15 years creditable service may apply for voluntary retirement with ministerial consent.
Second: If retired with under 15 years service, a lump-sum severance gratuity of 200% of final monthly salary per completed year of service is disbursed.

content.title: Pension Calculation Formula and Family Allowances
content.conditions:
First: The monthly pension is calculated by multiplying the last received salary by the number of completed pensionable months and dividing by 260.
Second: Monthly family allowances consist of 50,000 IQD for the spouse and 25,000 IQD per child for up to 5 children.
Third: Month and year fractions are rounded up to whole units.
Fourth: Under no circumstances may the pension exceed the final active salary.

content.title: End-of-Service Gratuity
content.conditions:
First: End-of-service gratuity is granted upon retirement as follows:
1. One year's full active salary for 15+ years of pre-March 5, 1991 service.
2. One year's full active salary for 20+ years overall creditable service.
Second: In all other eligible retirement cases, a gratuity equal to 6 months final salary is awarded.

content.title: Devolution of Rights to Surviving Heirs
content.conditions: Upon the death of a Peshmerga or pensioner, all pension entitlements, allowances, and accrued rights transfer to eligible statutory heirs.

content.title: Effective Date of Pension Disbursement
content.conditions: Pensions commence from date of discharge or death; delayed applications exceeding 3 years without lawful cause commence from application filing date.
content.formattedText: Article 31 > Effective Date of Pension Disbursement > Pensions commence from date of discharge or death; delayed applications exceeding 3 years without lawful cause commence from application filing date.

content.title: Option Between Pension and Civil Salary
content.conditions: If a pensioner is re-employed in a public civil office, he may elect between receiving his pension or active employment salary.
content.formattedText: Article 32 > Option Between Pension and Civil Salary > If a pensioner is re-employed in a public civil office, he may elect between receiving his pension or active employment salary.

content.title: Missing and Detained Personnel
content.conditions:
First: When a Peshmerga is missing or captured in duty, full salary continues to dependent heirs until return or verified decease.
Second: Pension is granted to heirs upon certified death or after 2 years of missing status, transferring records to Ministry of Martyrs.
Third: In cases of negligent desertion or ethical misconduct, legal prosecution and disciplinary retirement follow.
Fourth: The duration of captivity or missing status counts as active service.

content.title: Death and Martyrdom in the Line of Duty
content.conditions:
First: If a member dies in service with under 15 years service, creditable service is elevated to 15 years for full pension entitlement.
Second: Combat martyrs receive rights and honors under the Ministry of Martyrs and Anfal Affairs legislation.
Third: Pre-1991 continuous serving personnel are included.
Fourth: Files are transmitted to the Ministry of Martyrs.

Fourth: Files are transmitted to the Ministry of Martyrs.

content.title: Rights of Prisoners of War (POWs)
content.conditions:
First: Full salary, allowances, and emoluments are paid to dependents throughout captivity.
Second: The period of enemy captivity counts as actual active military service for all purposes.

Article 35 > Rights of Prisoners of War (POWs) > First: Full salary, allowances, and emoluments are paid to dependents throughout captivity.

content.title: Forfeiture of Pension for Treason
content.conditions: Pensioners or surviving heirs forfeit statutory pension entitlements upon established legal proof of treason or collaboration with hostile enemies of Kurdistan.
content.formattedText: Article 36 > Forfeiture of Pension for Treason > Pensioners or surviving heirs forfeit statutory pension entitlements upon established legal proof of treason or collaboration with hostile enemies of Kurdistan.

content.title: Recall of Pensioners and Gratuity
content.conditions: If a retiree is recalled to military duty by General Command order, retirement severance gratuity shall not be disbursed twice.
content.formattedText: Article 37 > Recall of Pensioners and Gratuity > If a retiree is recalled to military duty by General Command order, retirement severance gratuity shall not be disbursed twice.

content.title: Prohibition of Dual Official Salaries
content.conditions: No individual drawing a statutory Peshmerga pension may concurrently receive another official government salary.
content.formattedText: Article 38 > Prohibition of Dual Official Salaries > No individual drawing a statutory Peshmerga pension may concurrently receive another official government salary.

content.title: Pre-1991 Veterans Credited to 15 Years
content.conditions: Veterans joining the revolution pre-1991 with at least 3 years service are retired with credited 15 years service subject to: no other state salary, never opposed the revolution, uninterrupted service, and minimum age 16 at enlistment.
content.formattedText: Article 39 > Pre-1991 Veterans Credited to 15 Years > Veterans joining the revolution pre-1991 with at least 3 years service are retired with credited 15 years service subject to: no other state salary, never opposed the revolution, uninterrupted service, and minimum age 16 at enlistment.

content.title: Automatic Parity with Active Pay Scales
content.conditions: Whenever active service pay scales are upgraded, pensions automatically adjust in equal percentage by rank and post.
content.formattedText: Article 40 > Automatic Parity with Active Pay Scales > Whenever active service pay scales are upgraded, pensions automatically adjust in equal percentage by rank and post.

content.title: Assimilation of Existing Peshmerga Cadres
content.conditions: Personnel currently serving in Peshmerga forces are confirmed in their substantive ranks and entitled to full statutory retirement rights.
content.formattedText: Article 41 > Assimilation of Existing Peshmerga Cadres > Personnel currently serving in Peshmerga forces are confirmed in their substantive ranks and entitled to full statutory retirement rights.

content.title: Crediting Military College Studies
content.conditions: Graduation study periods in recognized military colleges/institutes count as creditable service for retirement purposes only.
content.formattedText: Article 42 > Crediting Military College Studies > Graduation study periods in recognized military colleges/institutes count as creditable service for retirement purposes only.

content.title: Non-Assignability and Seizure Limits
content.conditions:
First: Pension rights cannot be assigned or waived; any assignment is void ab initio.
Second: Attachment is barred except for court-ordered child/spousal support and debts due to Regional Treasury.
Third: In no case may attachment exceed 25% of monthly pension or gratuity.
content.formattedText:

content.title: Service Extension for Senior Officers
content.conditions: The Commander-in-Chief may extend the active service of senior officers, technicians, and specialists for up to 2 years for compelling public interest.
content.formattedText: Article 44 > Service Extension for Senior Officers > The Commander-in-Chief may extend the active service of senior officers, technicians, and specialists for up to 2 years for compelling public interest.

content.title: Exclusion of Former Regime Collaborators and War Criminals
content.conditions: This Law strictly excludes any individual legally proven to have collaborated with the repressive organs of the former regime or participated in Anfal and genocide crimes.
content.formattedText: Article 45 > Exclusion of Former Regime Collaborators and War Criminals > This Law strictly excludes any individual legally proven to have collaborated with the repressive organs of the former regime or participated in Anfal and genocide crimes.

content.title: Equality with Federal Armed Forces Standards
content.conditions: Peshmerga covered by this Law benefit from all rights, benefits, and privileges granted to counterparts in the federal Iraqi armed forces under federal law.
content.formattedText: Article 46 > Equality with Federal Armed Forces Standards > Peshmerga covered by this Law benefit from all rights, benefits, and privileges granted to counterparts in the federal Iraqi armed forces under federal law.

content.title: Prohibition of Partisan Political Activities
content.conditions: Partisan political activities and organizing within the ranks and formations of the Peshmerga forces are strictly prohibited.
content.formattedText: Article 47 > Prohibition of Partisan Political Activities > Partisan political activities and organizing within the ranks and formations of the Peshmerga forces are strictly prohibited.

content.title: Application to Kurdistan Citizens Outside the Region
content.conditions: Provisions of this Law extend to qualified citizens of Kurdistan residing outside the administrative boundaries of the Region.
content.formattedText: Article 48 > Application to Kurdistan Citizens Outside the Region > Provisions of this Law extend to qualified citizens of Kurdistan residing outside the administrative boundaries of the Region.

content.title: Supersession of Inconsistent Decisions
content.conditions: Any legal text, directive, or decision conflicting with the provisions of this Law is superseded and inapplicable.
content.formattedText: Article 49 > Supersession of Inconsistent Decisions > Any legal text, directive, or decision conflicting with the provisions of this Law is superseded and inapplicable.

content.formattedText: Article 50 > Cabinet Bylaw and Regulatory Mandate > The Council of Ministers and respective ministries are empowered to promulgate regulations and orders to execute this Law.

content.title: Scope of Application and Military Definitions
content.conditions:
First: The provisions of this Code apply to:
a. Active personnel of the Iraqi Armed Forces for crimes committed during or resulting from duty.
b. Cadets of military colleges, institutes, and service academies.
c. Retired, dismissed, or discharged officers, warrant officers, NCOs, and soldiers for crimes committed during active service.
d. Prisoners of war regarding offenses committed in detention camps.
e. Active reserve officers, NCOs, and enlisted personnel.
Second: Statutory Definitions: Officer (Lieutenant and above, including military Imams); Warrant Officer (Grades); NCO (Sergeants and Corporals); Private/Soldier (All enlisted servicemen); Army (Land, Naval, and Air forces); Unit/Detachment (Any formation under command of an officer).
content.formattedText:
Article 1 > Scope of Application and Military Definitions > First: The provisions of this Code apply to:
a. Active personnel of the Iraqi Armed Forces for crimes committed during or resulting from duty.
b. Cadets of military colleges, institutes, and service academies.
c. Retired, dismissed, or discharged officers, warrant officers, NCOs, and soldiers for crimes committed during active service.
d. Prisoners of war regarding offenses committed in detention camps.
e. Active reserve officers, NCOs, and enlisted personnel.
Second: Statutory Definitions: Officer (Lieutenant and above, including military Imams); Warrant Officer (Grades); NCO (Sergeants and Corporals); Private/Soldier (All enlisted servicemen); Army (Land, Naval, and Air forces); Unit/Detachment (Any formation under command of an officer).

content.title: Mobilization and State of Readiness
content.conditions:
First: Mobilization is the call-up of all or part of the military reserves into active service during external aggression or active operations.
Second: Mobilization commences upon the issuance of a written executive decree placing forces on mobilization and terminates upon its revocation.
Third: Military aircraft and naval vessels departing Iraqi territory in peacetime are deemed in a state of mobilization until return to base.
content.formattedText:

Second: Mobilization commences upon the issuance of a written executive decree placing forces on mobilization and terminates upon its revocation.
Third: Military aircraft and naval vessels departing Iraqi territory in peacetime are deemed in a state of mobilization until return to base.

content.title: Offenses Committed Outside Iraq
content.conditions: Offenses covered under this Code committed by military personnel abroad while on deployed forces, official missions, or study assignments are deemed committed in Iraq if not prosecuted in the foreign jurisdiction.
content.formattedText: Article 3 > Offenses Committed Outside Iraq > Offenses covered under this Code committed by military personnel abroad while on deployed forces, official missions, or study assignments are deemed committed in Iraq if not prosecuted in the foreign jurisdiction.

content.title: Prosecution of Prisoners of War under Geneva Conventions
content.conditions: Trials of prisoners of war before military tribunals shall proceed pursuant to the provisions of this Code and the Geneva Conventions relative to the Treatment of Prisoners of War.
content.formattedText: Article 4 > Prosecution of Prisoners of War under Geneva Conventions > Trials of prisoners of war before military tribunals shall proceed pursuant to the provisions of this Code and the Geneva Conventions relative to the Treatment of Prisoners of War.

content.title: Crimes Against Allied Forces
content.conditions:
First: Offenses committed against servicemen of allied nations during joint operations are treated as if committed against Iraqi personnel, subject to reciprocal international agreements.
Second: A serviceman refers to any person pursuing military service as an occupation.
content.formattedText:
Article 5 > Crimes Against Allied Forces > First: Offenses committed against servicemen of allied nations during joint operations are treated as if committed against Iraqi personnel, subject to reciprocal international agreements.
Second: A serviceman refers to any person pursuing military service as an occupation.

content.title: Facing the Enemy
content.conditions: All military formations, aircraft, and naval combatants are deemed facing the enemy from the commencement of tactical preparations for mobilization and battle.
content.formattedText: Article 6 > Facing the Enemy > All military formations, aircraft, and naval combatants are deemed facing the enemy from the commencement of tactical preparations for mobilization and battle.

content.title: Definitions of Enemy, Armed Status, Duty, and Commander
content.conditions:
Statutory Operational Terms:
First: Enemy: Any foreign state, hostile force, or armed insurgent group bearing arms against Iraq.
Second: Armed: Bearing arms for operational service or assembling armed under command.
Third: Duty/Service: Execution of specific military missions upon lawful superior orders.
Fourth: Commander: Person invested with command authority by law.
Fifth: Military Mutiny: Collective refusal to obey commands, violent resistance, or strike against military orders.
Sixth: Room Detention: Confinement of personnel inside dedicated quarters within camp limits.

content.title: Aggravating Circumstance in Troop Assembly
content.conditions: An offense is deemed aggravated if committed in an assembly before at least three military persons assembled for official service, excluding principals and accomplices.
content.formattedText: Article 8 > Aggravating Circumstance in Troop Assembly > An offense is deemed aggravated if committed in an assembly before at least three military persons assembled for official service, excluding principals and accomplices.

content.title: Definitions of Sentry and Guard Detail
content.conditions:
First: Sentry: An armed military serviceman stationed at a designated post to preserve security, surveillance, and order in peace or war.
Second: Guard Detail (Patrol): One or more armed servicemen under command detailed for statutory security missions.
content.formattedText:
Article 9 > Definitions of Sentry and Guard Detail > First: Sentry: An armed military serviceman stationed at a designated post to preserve security, surveillance, and order in peace or war.
Second: Guard Detail (Patrol): One or more armed servicemen under command detailed for statutory security missions.

content.title: Classification of Primary Penalties
content.conditions:
Primary statutory penalties comprise:
1. Execution: Capital punishment inflicted by firing squad.
2. Life Imprisonment: Confinement for a period of twenty years.
3. Temporary Imprisonment: Confinement from over 5 years up to 15 years.
4. Severe Confinement: Incarceration from over 3 months up to 5 years with hard labor.
5. Simple Confinement: Incarceration from 24 hours up to 3 years.

4. Severe Confinement: Incarceration from over 3 months up to 5 years with hard labor.
5. Simple Confinement: Incarceration from 24 hours up to 3 years.

content.title: Fines and Seniority Deduction for Officers
content.conditions: For offenses punishable by confinement not exceeding 3 years, an officer may be sentenced to a fine or loss of seniority not exceeding 2 years in lieu of imprisonment upon mitigating grounds, excluding dishonorable offenses.
content.formattedText: Article 11 > Fines and Seniority Deduction for Officers > For offenses punishable by confinement not exceeding 3 years, an officer may be sentenced to a fine or loss of seniority not exceeding 2 years in lieu of imprisonment upon mitigating grounds, excluding dishonorable offenses.

content.title: Barracks Confinement Rules and Limits
content.conditions: Barracks confinement may be imposed on officers for up to 15 days, and on warrant officers, NCOs, and privates for up to 30 days; it shall not be imposed on academy cadets.
content.formattedText: Article 12 > Barracks Confinement Rules and Limits > Barracks confinement may be imposed on officers for up to 15 days, and on warrant officers, NCOs, and privates for up to 30 days; it shall not be imposed on academy cadets.

content.title: Regime of Barracks Confinement
content.conditions: Personnel sentenced to barracks confinement are not exempt from routine duty or field parade, are barred from leaving military premises, and cannot receive visitors except on service necessity.
content.formattedText: Article 13 > Regime of Barracks Confinement > Personnel sentenced to barracks confinement are not exempt from routine duty or field parade, are barred from leaving military premises, and cannot receive visitors except on service necessity.

content.title: Salary Rights During Barracks Confinement
content.conditions: Personnel undergoing barracks confinement remain entitled to their full salaries and allowances during confinement.
content.formattedText: Article 14 > Salary Rights During Barracks Confinement > Personnel undergoing barracks confinement remain entitled to their full salaries and allowances during confinement.

content.title: Mandatory and Discretionary Expulsion/Discharge
content.conditions:
First: Expulsion from service or contract annulment is mandatory upon conviction to death, life or temporary imprisonment, terrorism offenses, dishonorable crimes, or rape and sexual assaults.
Second: The military tribunal may discretionary order expulsion upon conviction to simple confinement.
Third: An officer shall be cashiered if he forfeits any mandatory condition of his appointment.
content.formattedText:
Article 15 > Mandatory and Discretionary Expulsion/Discharge > First: Expulsion from service or contract annulment is mandatory upon conviction to death, life or temporary imprisonment, terrorism offenses, dishonorable crimes, or rape and sexual assaults.
Second: The military tribunal may discretionary order expulsion upon conviction to simple confinement.
Third: An officer shall be cashiered if he forfeits any mandatory condition of his appointment.

content.title: Legal Consequences of Cashiering and Expulsion
content.conditions: Expulsion entails forfeiture of military rank, decorations, medals, and absolute lifetime disqualification from re-enlisting in the armed forces.
content.formattedText: Article 16 > Legal Consequences of Cashiering and Expulsion > Expulsion entails forfeiture of military rank, decorations, medals, and absolute lifetime disqualification from re-enlisting in the armed forces.

content.title: Rank Reduction of NCOs and Warrant Officers
content.conditions: The tribunal may reduce a non-commissioned officer or warrant officer to a subordinate grade or to the rank of private for punishable offenses.
content.formattedText: Article 17 > Rank Reduction of NCOs and Warrant Officers > The tribunal may reduce a non-commissioned officer or warrant officer to a subordinate grade or to the rank of private for punishable offenses.

content.title: Forfeiture of Commission and Rank
content.conditions: Forfeiture of rank deprives the officer of his commission and status, relegating him to civilian standing without military privileges.
content.formattedText: Article 18 > Forfeiture of Commission and Rank > Forfeiture of rank deprives the officer of his commission and status, relegating him to civilian standing without military privileges.

content.title: Salary Stoppages and Deductions
content.conditions: Deductions from pay may be awarded as a disciplinary sanction, not exceeding one-third (1/3) of monthly pay for the awarded term.
content.formattedText: Article 19 > Salary Stoppages and Deductions > Deductions from pay may be awarded as a disciplinary sanction, not exceeding one-third (1/3) of monthly pay for the awarded term.

content.title: Reprimand and Severe Reprimand
content.conditions: Reprimand and severe reprimand are entered in writing in the service record, legally retarding eligibility for promotion and step increases.
content.formattedText: Article 20 > Reprimand and Severe Reprimand > Reprimand and severe reprimand are entered in writing in the service record, legally retarding eligibility for promotion and step increases.

content.title: Extra Guard and Drill Duties
content.conditions: Extra guard watch, fatigues, and disciplinary drills may be awarded to enlisted personnel pursuant to military command bylaws.
content.formattedText: Article 21 > Extra Guard and Drill Duties > Extra guard watch, fatigues, and disciplinary drills may be awarded to enlisted personnel pursuant to military command bylaws.

content.title: Execution of Sentences in Military Prisons
content.conditions: Sentences of confinement are executed within military prisons and garrison detention centers pursuant to Ministry of Defense regulations.
content.formattedText: Article 22 > Execution of Sentences in Military Prisons > Sentences of confinement are executed within military prisons and garrison detention centers pursuant to Ministry of Defense regulations.

content.title: Deduction of Pre-Trial Remand from Sentence
content.conditions: Pre-trial detention and custody served prior to final judgment shall be fully deducted from the term of imprisonment imposed.
content.formattedText: Article 23 > Deduction of Pre-Trial Remand from Sentence > Pre-trial detention and custody served prior to final judgment shall be fully deducted from the term of imprisonment imposed.

content.title: Plurality of Offenses and Sentence Aggregation
content.conditions: Where multiple related offenses are committed, the tribunal imposes the penalty prescribed for the gravest offense unless cumulative execution is statutory.
content.formattedText: Article 24 > Plurality of Offenses and Sentence Aggregation > Where multiple related offenses are committed, the tribunal imposes the penalty prescribed for the gravest offense unless cumulative execution is statutory.

content.title: Mitigating and Aggravating Factors in Military Justice
content.conditions: Military tribunals evaluate valor in combat, prior disciplinary record, battlefield conditions, and aggravating or mitigating factors in sentencing.
content.formattedText: Article 25 > Mitigating and Aggravating Factors in Military Justice > Military tribunals evaluate valor in combat, prior disciplinary record, battlefield conditions, and aggravating or mitigating factors in sentencing.

content.title: Prohibition of Suspended Sentences for Grave Offenses
content.conditions: Stay or suspension of sentence execution is barred for offenses of high treason, armed mutiny, desertion facing the enemy, or ammunition theft.
content.formattedText: Article 26 > Prohibition of Suspended Sentences for Grave Offenses > Stay or suspension of sentence execution is barred for offenses of high treason, armed mutiny, desertion facing the enemy, or ammunition theft.

content.title: High Treason and Bearing Arms Against the State
content.conditions: Capital punishment (death) applies to any serviceman who bears arms against Iraq or joins hostile enemy forces in time of war or mobilization.
content.formattedText: Article 27 > High Treason and Bearing Arms Against the State > Capital punishment (death) applies to any serviceman who bears arms against Iraq or joins hostile enemy forces in time of war or mobilization.

content.title: Surrender of Fortifications and Units to the Enemy
content.conditions: Death penalty applies to any commander who surrenders a fortress, position, vessel, or combat aircraft to the enemy without exhausting all defense.
content.formattedText: Article 28 > Surrender of Fortifications and Units to the Enemy > Death penalty applies to any commander who surrenders a fortress, position, vessel, or combat aircraft to the enemy without exhausting all defense.

content.title: Espionage and Leaking Military Secrets
content.conditions: Death penalty applies to any serviceman engaging in espionage, intelligence disclosure, or delivering defense operational secrets to foreign powers.
content.formattedText: Article 29 > Espionage and Leaking Military Secrets > Death penalty applies to any serviceman engaging in espionage, intelligence disclosure, or delivering defense operational secrets to foreign powers.

content.title: Demoralization and Spreading Panic During Operations
content.conditions: Punishable by death or life imprisonment: causing panic, defeatism, or inciting retreat among troops in the field facing the enemy.
content.formattedText: Article 30 > Demoralization and Spreading Panic During Operations > Punishable by death or life imprisonment: causing panic, defeatism, or inciting retreat among troops in the field facing the enemy.

content.title: Sabotage of Military Installations and Defenses
content.conditions: Death penalty is incurred for intentional sabotage of military installations, communication links, supply lines, or ammunition dumps.
content.formattedText: Article 31 > Sabotage of Military Installations and Defenses > Death penalty is incurred for intentional sabotage of military installations, communication links, supply lines, or ammunition dumps.

content.title: Harboring Enemy Spies and Facilitating Escape
content.conditions: Punishable by life or temporary imprisonment: harboring, concealing, or aiding the escape of enemy spies or combatants.
content.formattedText: Article 32 > Harboring Enemy Spies and Facilitating Escape > Punishable by life or temporary imprisonment: harboring, concealing, or aiding the escape of enemy spies or combatants.

content.title: Illicit Commercial Dealing with the Enemy
content.conditions: Punishable by temporary imprisonment: conducting trade, supply transfers, or financial transactions with the enemy during war.
content.formattedText: Article 33 > Illicit Commercial Dealing with the Enemy > Punishable by temporary imprisonment: conducting trade, supply transfers, or financial transactions with the enemy during war.

content.title: Plundering Wounded and Deceased in Combat
content.conditions: Imprisonment up to 10 years for pillaging, stripping possessions, or robbing wounded soldiers or war dead on the battlefield.
content.formattedText: Article 34 > Plundering Wounded and Deceased in Combat > Imprisonment up to 10 years for pillaging, stripping possessions, or robbing wounded soldiers or war dead on the battlefield.

content.title: Failure of Commander to Relieve Besieged Friendly Forces
content.conditions: Death or life imprisonment for a commander who intentionally fails to relieve or support engaged friendly troops when capable of intervention.
content.formattedText: Article 35 > Failure of Commander to Relieve Besieged Friendly Forces > Death or life imprisonment for a commander who intentionally fails to relieve or support engaged friendly troops when capable of intervention.

content.title: Military Mutiny in Peace and War
content.conditions: Capital punishment applies to ringleaders and inciters of mutiny facing the enemy; temporary imprisonment applies if mutiny occurs in peacetime.
content.formattedText: Article 36 > Military Mutiny in Peace and War > Capital punishment applies to ringleaders and inciters of mutiny facing the enemy; temporary imprisonment applies if mutiny occurs in peacetime.

content.title: Incitement to Mutiny and Failure to Suppress Mutiny
content.conditions: Punishable by imprisonment: failure by an officer aware of a mutinous conspiracy to suppress it immediately or report it to higher headquarters.
content.formattedText: Article 37 > Incitement to Mutiny and Failure to Suppress Mutiny > Punishable by imprisonment: failure by an officer aware of a mutinous conspiracy to suppress it immediately or report it to higher headquarters.

content.title: Refusal of Direct Lawful Orders During Operations
content.conditions: Imprisonment for not less than 7 years for refusing a direct lawful command relating to tactical field duties during operations or mobilization.
content.formattedText: Article 38 > Refusal of Direct Lawful Orders During Operations > Imprisonment for not less than 7 years for refusing a direct lawful command relating to tactical field duties during operations or mobilization.

content.title: Refusal of Lawful Orders in Peacetime
content.conditions: Severe confinement up to 3 years for intentionally disobeying a lawful command issued by a military superior in peacetime.
content.formattedText: Article 39 > Refusal of Lawful Orders in Peacetime > Severe confinement up to 3 years for intentionally disobeying a lawful command issued by a military superior in peacetime.

content.title: Collective Unlawful Petitions and Grievances
content.conditions: Confinement up to 1 year for organizing, signing, or presenting collective grievances in violation of military service channels.
content.formattedText: Article 40 > Collective Unlawful Petitions and Grievances > Confinement up to 1 year for organizing, signing, or presenting collective grievances in violation of military service channels.

content.title: Contempt and Desecration of National and Military Flags
content.conditions: Confinement up to 3 years for publicly insulting or showing contempt toward the national flag or armed forces emblems.
content.formattedText: Article 41 > Contempt and Desecration of National and Military Flags > Confinement up to 3 years for publicly insulting or showing contempt toward the national flag or armed forces emblems.

content.title: Desertion to the Enemy
content.conditions: Mandatory capital punishment by firing squad applies to any serviceman who deserts to or crosses over to the enemy.
content.formattedText: Article 42 > Desertion to the Enemy > Mandatory capital punishment by firing squad applies to any serviceman who deserts to or crosses over to the enemy.

content.title: Desertion in the Face of the Enemy
content.conditions: Death or life imprisonment for abandoning one's post or deserting in the face of the enemy during tactical engagement.
content.formattedText: Article 43 > Desertion in the Face of the Enemy > Death or life imprisonment for abandoning one's post or deserting in the face of the enemy during tactical engagement.

content.title: Desertion During Mobilization
content.conditions: Imprisonment from 7 to 15 years for deserting military service during proclaimed mobilization or national emergency.
content.formattedText: Article 44 > Desertion During Mobilization > Imprisonment from 7 to 15 years for deserting military service during proclaimed mobilization or national emergency.

content.title: Desertion in Peacetime
content.conditions: Severe confinement from 1 to 5 years for deserting military service in peacetime.
content.formattedText: Article 45 > Desertion in Peacetime > Severe confinement from 1 to 5 years for deserting military service in peacetime.

content.title: Conspiracy and Collective Desertion
content.conditions: Imprisonment up to 10 years for collective desertion planned or executed jointly by two or more servicemen.
content.formattedText: Article 46 > Conspiracy and Collective Desertion > Imprisonment up to 10 years for collective desertion planned or executed jointly by two or more servicemen.

content.title: Desertion with Weapons, Aircraft, or Vessels
content.conditions: Imprisonment from 7 to 15 years for deserting military duty while carrying military weapons, combat vehicles, or aircraft.
content.formattedText: Article 47 > Desertion with Weapons, Aircraft, or Vessels > Imprisonment from 7 to 15 years for deserting military duty while carrying military weapons, combat vehicles, or aircraft.

content.title: Absence Without Official Leave (AWOL)
content.conditions: Confinement up to 3 years for unauthorized absence exceeding 15 days in peace or 5 days during mobilization.
content.formattedText: Article 48 > Absence Without Official Leave (AWOL) > Confinement up to 3 years for unauthorized absence exceeding 15 days in peace or 5 days during mobilization.

content.title: Concealing and Assisting Military Deserters
content.conditions: Confinement up to 2 years for knowingly harboring, concealing, or aiding a military deserter to evade arrest.
content.formattedText: Article 49 > Concealing and Assisting Military Deserters > Confinement up to 2 years for knowingly harboring, concealing, or aiding a military deserter to evade arrest.

content.title: Intentional Self-Mutilation and Malingering
content.conditions: Imprisonment up to 7 years for intentionally inflicting self-mutilation, inducing disease, or malingering to evade military obligations.
content.formattedText: Article 50 > Intentional Self-Mutilation and Malingering > Imprisonment up to 7 years for intentionally inflicting self-mutilation, inducing disease, or malingering to evade military obligations.

content.title: Assaulting a Military Superior on Duty
content.conditions: Imprisonment up to 7 years for physically assaulting a military superior in the execution of his duty or because of his status.
content.formattedText: Article 51 > Assaulting a Military Superior on Duty > Imprisonment up to 7 years for physically assaulting a military superior in the execution of his duty or because of his status.

content.title: Aggravated Assault Causing Death of Superior
content.conditions: Death or life imprisonment if physical assault upon a military superior results in death or permanent bodily infirmity.
content.formattedText: Article 52 > Aggravated Assault Causing Death of Superior > Death or life imprisonment if physical assault upon a military superior results in death or permanent bodily infirmity.

content.title: Threatening Superiors with Weapons
content.conditions: Imprisonment from 5 to 10 years for threatening a military superior by brandishing or pointing firearms.
content.formattedText: Article 53 > Threatening Superiors with Weapons > Imprisonment from 5 to 10 years for threatening a military superior by brandishing or pointing firearms.

content.title: Insulting and Defaming Military Superiors
content.conditions: Confinement up to 3 years for verbally insulting, defaming, or making threatening gestures toward a military superior.
content.formattedText: Article 54 > Insulting and Defaming Military Superiors > Confinement up to 3 years for verbally insulting, defaming, or making threatening gestures toward a military superior.

content.title: Abuse of Command Authority Against Subordinates
content.conditions: Confinement up to 3 years for a superior who abuses command authority by striking or mistreating subordinates unlawfully.
content.formattedText: Article 55 > Abuse of Command Authority Against Subordinates > Confinement up to 3 years for a superior who abuses command authority by striking or mistreating subordinates unlawfully.

content.title: Compelling Personnel to Perform Unlawful or Personal Tasks
content.conditions: Confinement up to 2 years for ordering or compelling subordinate soldiers to render personal services outside official duties.
content.formattedText: Article 56 > Compelling Personnel to Perform Unlawful or Personal Tasks > Confinement up to 2 years for ordering or compelling subordinate soldiers to render personal services outside official duties.

content.title: Brawling and Violent Assault Between Peers
content.conditions: Confinement up to 2 years for brawling, mutual violence, or assaulting colleagues of equal rank in uniform or quarters.
content.formattedText: Article 57 > Brawling and Violent Assault Between Peers > Confinement up to 2 years for brawling, mutual violence, or assaulting colleagues of equal rank in uniform or quarters.

content.title: Failure to Suppress Disorder or Violence Among Troops
content.conditions: Confinement up to 1 year for any military superior failing to intervene immediately to quell violent altercations occurring in his presence.
content.formattedText: Article 58 > Failure to Suppress Disorder or Violence Among Troops > Confinement up to 1 year for any military superior failing to intervene immediately to quell violent altercations occurring in his presence.

content.title: Filing Vexatious, Malicious, or Fraudulent Complaints
content.conditions: Confinement up to 2 years for knowingly submitting malicious, false, or defamatory accusations against superiors or peers.
content.formattedText: Article 59 > Filing Vexatious, Malicious, or Fraudulent Complaints > Confinement up to 2 years for knowingly submitting malicious, false, or defamatory accusations against superiors or peers.

content.title: Bribery, Extortion, and Influence Peddling
content.conditions: Imprisonment up to 10 years for soliciting or taking bribes or unlawful benefits for granting leaves, transfers, or duty dispensations.
content.formattedText: Article 60 > Bribery, Extortion, and Influence Peddling > Imprisonment up to 10 years for soliciting or taking bribes or unlawful benefits for granting leaves, transfers, or duty dispensations.

content.title: Theft and Embezzlement of Military Arms and Ammunition
content.conditions: Imprisonment for not less than 7 years for theft, misappropriation, or embezzlement of statutory arms, ordnance, or munitions.
content.formattedText: Article 61 > Theft and Embezzlement of Military Arms and Ammunition > Imprisonment for not less than 7 years for theft, misappropriation, or embezzlement of statutory arms, ordnance, or munitions.

content.title: Selling, Pawning, or Illicitly Disposing of Military Arms
content.conditions: Imprisonment up to 15 years for selling, pawning, pledging, or disposing of military weapons or ammunition entrusted for service.
content.formattedText: Article 62 > Selling, Pawning, or Illicitly Disposing of Military Arms > Imprisonment up to 15 years for selling, pawning, pledging, or disposing of military weapons or ammunition entrusted for service.

content.title: Negligent Loss or Damage to Weapons and Gear
content.conditions: Confinement up to 3 years and financial restitution for negligently losing, damaging, or failing to maintain assigned weapons and equipment.
content.formattedText: Article 63 > Negligent Loss or Damage to Weapons and Gear > Confinement up to 3 years and financial restitution for negligently losing, damaging, or failing to maintain assigned weapons and equipment.

content.title: Embezzlement of Military Rations, Fuel, and Funds
content.conditions: Imprisonment for not less than 5 years and restitution of double the value for embezzling rations, fuel, medical stores, or army funds.
content.formattedText: Article 64 > Embezzlement of Military Rations, Fuel, and Funds > Imprisonment for not less than 5 years and restitution of double the value for embezzling rations, fuel, medical stores, or army funds.

content.title: Arson and Destruction of Military Depots
content.conditions: Death or life imprisonment for intentionally setting fire to, exploding, or destroying munitions depots or armed forces installations.
content.formattedText: Article 65 > Arson and Destruction of Military Depots > Death or life imprisonment for intentionally setting fire to, exploding, or destroying munitions depots or armed forces installations.

content.title: Negligent Discharge of Explosives and Munitions
content.conditions: Imprisonment up to 7 years for causing an explosion or detonation of ammunition depots through criminal negligence or disregard of safety.
content.formattedText: Article 66 > Negligent Discharge of Explosives and Munitions > Imprisonment up to 7 years for causing an explosion or detonation of ammunition depots through criminal negligence or disregard of safety.

content.title: Unlawful Driving and Misuse of Military Vehicles
content.conditions: Confinement up to 1 year and restitution of operational damages for driving military vehicles without authorization or for private uses.
content.formattedText: Article 67 > Unlawful Driving and Misuse of Military Vehicles > Confinement up to 1 year and restitution of operational damages for driving military vehicles without authorization or for private uses.

content.title: Forgery in Military Muster Rolls and Rations Registers
content.conditions: Imprisonment for not less than 5 years for falsifying or forging military personnel rolls, pay registers, or ammunition delivery vouchers.
content.formattedText: Article 68 > Forgery in Military Muster Rolls and Rations Registers > Imprisonment for not less than 5 years for falsifying or forging military personnel rolls, pay registers, or ammunition delivery vouchers.

content.title: Collusion and Accepting Defective Military Gear
content.conditions: Imprisonment for not less than 7 years for procurement board members accepting defective weapons, expired rations, or unapproved military supplies.
content.formattedText: Article 69 > Collusion and Accepting Defective Military Gear > Imprisonment for not less than 7 years for procurement board members accepting defective weapons, expired rations, or unapproved military supplies.

content.title: Statutory Restitution to the Defense Treasury
content.conditions: The military tribunal shall order mandatory return of stolen or embezzled items and full restitution of damages to the defense treasury.
content.formattedText: Article 70 > Statutory Restitution to the Defense Treasury > The military tribunal shall order mandatory return of stolen or embezzled items and full restitution of damages to the defense treasury.

content.title: Sleeping on Guard Post Facing the Enemy
content.conditions: Death or life imprisonment for a sentry found asleep at his post while facing the enemy or on forward tactical contact lines.
content.formattedText: Article 71 > Sleeping on Guard Post Facing the Enemy > Death or life imprisonment for a sentry found asleep at his post while facing the enemy or on forward tactical contact lines.

content.title: Sleeping on Sentry Duty in Peacetime
content.conditions: Confinement up to 2 years for a sentry sleeping while on guard watch within military quarters in peacetime.
content.formattedText: Article 72 > Sleeping on Sentry Duty in Peacetime > Confinement up to 2 years for a sentry sleeping while on guard watch within military quarters in peacetime.

content.title: Abandoning Guard Post Without Proper Relief
content.conditions: Imprisonment up to 10 years for abandoning a guard post in wartime; severe confinement up to 3 years in peacetime.
content.formattedText: Article 73 > Abandoning Guard Post Without Proper Relief > Imprisonment up to 10 years for abandoning a guard post in wartime; severe confinement up to 3 years in peacetime.

content.title: Intoxication and Drug Use While on Duty
content.conditions: Severe confinement up to 5 years for being found intoxicated or under the influence of narcotics while performing military duty or watch.
content.formattedText: Article 74 > Intoxication and Drug Use While on Duty > Severe confinement up to 5 years for being found intoxicated or under the influence of narcotics while performing military duty or watch.

content.title: Breaching Prohibited Military Zones and Installations
content.conditions: Confinement up to 2 years for unlawfully entering restricted military zones or permitting unauthorized persons into secure installations.
content.formattedText: Article 75 > Breaching Prohibited Military Zones and Installations > Confinement up to 2 years for unlawfully entering restricted military zones or permitting unauthorized persons into secure installations.

content.title: Divulging Countersigns and Passwords
content.conditions: Imprisonment up to 10 years for disclosing passwords, countersigns, or recognition signals to unauthorized personnel.
content.formattedText: Article 76 > Divulging Countersigns and Passwords > Imprisonment up to 10 years for disclosing passwords, countersigns, or recognition signals to unauthorized personnel.

content.title: Tampering with Maps and Tactical Situation Reports
content.conditions: Imprisonment for not less than 7 years for intentionally forging, manipulating, or misreporting tactical battle maps or situation reports.
content.formattedText: Article 77 > Tampering with Maps and Tactical Situation Reports > Imprisonment for not less than 7 years for intentionally forging, manipulating, or misreporting tactical battle maps or situation reports.

content.title: Forging Military IDs, Travel Passes, and Movement Orders
content.conditions: Imprisonment up to 7 years for counterfeiting military identity cards, vehicle passes, movement orders, or tactical travel permits.
content.formattedText: Article 78 > Forging Military IDs, Travel Passes, and Movement Orders > Imprisonment up to 7 years for counterfeiting military identity cards, vehicle passes, movement orders, or tactical travel permits.

content.title: Subsidiary Application of General Iraqi Penal Code
content.conditions: Provisions of Iraqi Penal Code No. 111 of 1969 as amended apply to all matters and offenses not expressly regulated under this Code.
content.formattedText: Article 79 > Subsidiary Application of General Iraqi Penal Code > Provisions of Iraqi Penal Code No. 111 of 1969 as amended apply to all matters and offenses not expressly regulated under this Code.

content.title: Civil Liability and Restitution Claims
content.conditions: Imposition of military penal sanctions does not bar civil tort liability or claims for financial damages brought by aggrieved parties.
content.formattedText: Article 80 > Civil Liability and Restitution Claims > Imposition of military penal sanctions does not bar civil tort liability or claims for financial damages brought by aggrieved parties.

content.title: Repeal of Former Military Penal Legislation
content.conditions: Military Penal Code No. 13 of 1940 and all amendments thereto are hereby repealed and replaced by this Code.
content.formattedText: Article 81 > Repeal of Former Military Penal Legislation > Military Penal Code No. 13 of 1940 and all amendments thereto are hereby repealed and replaced by this Code.

content.title: Issuance of Executive Regulations by Minister of Defense
content.conditions: The Minister of Defense is authorized to issue directives and internal regulations to facilitate the enforcement of this Code.
content.formattedText: Article 82 > Issuance of Executive Regulations by Minister of Defense > The Minister of Defense is authorized to issue directives and internal regulations to facilitate the enforcement of this Code.

content.title: Effective Date and Gazette Publication
content.conditions: This Code shall enter into force from the date of its publication in the Iraqi Official Gazette (Al-Waqaei Al-Iraqiya) No. 4040 on May 9, 2007.
content.formattedText: Article 83 > Effective Date and Gazette Publication > This Code shall enter into force from the date of its publication in the Iraqi Official Gazette (Al-Waqaei Al-Iraqiya) No. 4040 on May 9, 2007.

content.title: Scope of Application
content.conditions: The provisions of this Code apply to all military personnel governed under Military Penal Code No. 19 of 2007 as amended, and to prisoners of war.
content.formattedText: Article 1 > Scope of Application > The provisions of this Code apply to all military personnel governed under Military Penal Code No. 19 of 2007 as amended, and to prisoners of war.

content.title: Composition and Structure of Military Courts
Types of Military Trials (Summary and Non-Summary)
Independence of the Military Judiciary
content.conditions: Military judges are independent and subject to no authority in their judicial determinations other than the law and conscience.
content.formattedText: Article 4 > Independence of the Military Judiciary > Military judges are independent and subject to no authority in their judicial determinations other than the law and conscience.

content.title: Territorial and Subject-Matter Jurisdiction
content.conditions: Military courts possess subject-matter and territorial jurisdiction over crimes under the Military Penal Code committed by military subjects inside or outside Iraq.
content.formattedText: Article 5 > Territorial and Subject-Matter Jurisdiction > Military courts possess subject-matter and territorial jurisdiction over crimes under the Military Penal Code committed by military subjects inside or outside Iraq.

content.title: Subsidiary Application of General Criminal Procedure
content.conditions: Provisions of the General Criminal Procedure Code No. 23 of 1971 as amended apply supplementary to all matters not expressly provided herein.
content.formattedText: Article 6 > Subsidiary Application of General Criminal Procedure > Provisions of the General Criminal Procedure Code No. 23 of 1971 as amended apply supplementary to all matters not expressly provided herein.

content.title: Article 7 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers
content.conditions: Every serviceman who gains knowledge of a military crime must immediately inform his direct commanding officer or the military investigator.
content.formattedText: Article 7 > Article 7 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers > Every serviceman who gains knowledge of a military crime must immediately inform his direct commanding officer or the military investigator.

content.title: Article 8 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers
content.conditions: In unnatural deaths, suspected homicides, or suicides within military units, the commander and investigator inspect the locus and order an autopsy.
content.formattedText: Article 8 > Article 8 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers > In unnatural deaths, suspected homicides, or suicides within military units, the commander and investigator inspect the locus and order an autopsy.

content.title: Article 9 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers
content.conditions: Military investigative and intelligence officers exercise judicial police powers to secure crime scenes, preserve evidence, and seize exhibits.
content.formattedText: Article 9 > Article 9 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers > Military investigative and intelligence officers exercise judicial police powers to secure crime scenes, preserve evidence, and seize exhibits.

content.title: Article 10 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers
content.conditions: The commanding officer forms a 3-officer Investigative Board chaired by the senior officer to establish facts, examine witnesses, and recommend action.
content.formattedText: Article 10 > Article 10 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers > The commanding officer forms a 3-officer Investigative Board chaired by the senior officer to establish facts, examine witnesses, and recommend action.

content.title: Article 11 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers
content.conditions: The accused serviceman must be informed of the charges at the outset of interrogation and possesses the right to remain silent without prejudice.
content.formattedText: Article 11 > Article 11 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers > The accused serviceman must be informed of the charges at the outset of interrogation and possesses the right to remain silent without prejudice.

content.title: Article 12 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers
content.conditions: The accused has the right to legal counsel during preliminary investigations in felony cases; appointed counsel is designated if unrepresented.
content.formattedText: Article 12 > Article 12 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers > The accused has the right to legal counsel during preliminary investigations in felony cases; appointed counsel is designated if unrepresented.

content.title: Article 13 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers
content.conditions: Physical and psychological torture and coercion are strictly prohibited; confessions obtained under duress or torture are null and void.
content.formattedText: Article 13 > Article 13 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers > Physical and psychological torture and coercion are strictly prohibited; confessions obtained under duress or torture are null and void.

content.title: Article 14 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers
content.conditions: Depositions of witnesses and technical military experts are recorded under oath before the investigator and signed into the official record.
content.formattedText: Article 14 > Article 14 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers > Depositions of witnesses and technical military experts are recorded under oath before the investigator and signed into the official record.

content.title: Article 15 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers
content.conditions: Search of a serviceman's residence or personal quarters requires a judicial search warrant issued by the competent military judge.
content.formattedText: Article 15 > Article 15 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers > Search of a serviceman's residence or personal quarters requires a judicial search warrant issued by the competent military judge.

content.title: Article 16 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers
content.conditions: Seized weapons and material evidence are labeled, cataloged, attached to the dossier, and lodged in the evidence locker of the court.
content.formattedText: Article 16 > Article 16 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers > Seized weapons and material evidence are labeled, cataloged, attached to the dossier, and lodged in the evidence locker of the court.

content.title: Article 17 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers
content.conditions: The investigator may order medical examinations of the accused or victim to verify injuries, intoxication, or toxicology.
content.formattedText: Article 17 > Article 17 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers > The investigator may order medical examinations of the accused or victim to verify injuries, intoxication, or toxicology.

content.title: Article 18 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers
content.conditions: The Military Public Prosecution oversees the legality of the investigation, attends interrogations, and lodges appropriate petitions.
content.formattedText: Article 18 > Article 18 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers > The Military Public Prosecution oversees the legality of the investigation, attends interrogations, and lodges appropriate petitions.

content.title: Article 19 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers
content.conditions: Investigation deadlines may be extended during combat operations by a reasoned decision of the military judge if battles preclude timely completion.
content.formattedText: Article 19 > Article 19 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers > Investigation deadlines may be extended during combat operations by a reasoned decision of the military judge if battles preclude timely completion.

content.title: Article 20 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers
content.conditions: The investigator may conduct confrontational examinations between co-defendants or witnesses to resolve evidentiary discrepancies.
content.formattedText: Article 20 > Article 20 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers > The investigator may conduct confrontational examinations between co-defendants or witnesses to resolve evidentiary discrepancies.

content.title: Article 21 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers
content.conditions: The preliminary investigation closes by judicial order either dismissing the charge for lack of evidence or referring the defendant to trial.
content.formattedText: Article 21 > Article 21 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers > The preliminary investigation closes by judicial order either dismissing the charge for lack of evidence or referring the defendant to trial.

content.title: Article 22 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers
content.conditions: In multi-unit jurisdictional conflicts, the Military Justice Directorate resolves the venue and assigns the competent investigative body.
content.formattedText: Article 22 > Article 22 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers > In multi-unit jurisdictional conflicts, the Military Justice Directorate resolves the venue and assigns the competent investigative body.

content.title: Article 23 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers
content.conditions: Military investigative boards may requisition records and official documents directly from civil state ministries and agencies.
content.formattedText: Article 23 > Article 23 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers > Military investigative boards may requisition records and official documents directly from civil state ministries and agencies.

content.title: Article 24 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers
content.conditions: Military preliminary investigation proceedings constitute classified defense records; unauthorized leaks trigger severe penal liability.
content.formattedText: Article 24 > Article 24 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers > Military preliminary investigation proceedings constitute classified defense records; unauthorized leaks trigger severe penal liability.

content.title: Article 25 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers
