content.conditions: Upon conclusion of the investigation, the dossier together with the prosecution's brief is submitted to the referral authority.
content.formattedText: Article 25 > Article 25 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers > Upon conclusion of the investigation, the dossier together with the prosecution's brief is submitted to the referral authority.

content.title: Article 26 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols
content.conditions: An arrest warrant against a military suspect is issued through a reasoned warrant signed by the military judge or referral authority.
content.formattedText: Article 26 > Article 26 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols > An arrest warrant against a military suspect is issued through a reasoned warrant signed by the military judge or referral authority.

content.title: Article 27 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols
content.conditions: Any officer or serviceman may arrest a military suspect caught flagrante delicto (in the act) and deliver him to the nearest command post.
content.formattedText: Article 27 > Article 27 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols > Any officer or serviceman may arrest a military suspect caught flagrante delicto (in the act) and deliver him to the nearest command post.

content.title: Article 28 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols
content.conditions: An arrested serviceman must be presented before the military judge within 24 hours of arrest to decide on remand or release.
content.formattedText: Article 28 > Article 28 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols > An arrested serviceman must be presented before the military judge within 24 hours of arrest to decide on remand or release.

content.title: Article 29 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols
content.conditions: The military judge may remand the accused for up to 15 days at a time, not exceeding 6 months aggregate except by cassation decree.
content.formattedText: Article 29 > Article 29 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols > The military judge may remand the accused for up to 15 days at a time, not exceeding 6 months aggregate except by cassation decree.

content.title: Article 30 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols
content.conditions: Military detainees are held in dedicated garrison remand facilities segregating officers from NCOs and enlisted personnel.
content.formattedText: Article 30 > Article 30 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols > Military detainees are held in dedicated garrison remand facilities segregating officers from NCOs and enlisted personnel.

content.title: Article 31 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols
content.conditions: Release on bail or personal surety is permissible for misdemeanors unless detention is required for operational integrity.
content.formattedText: Article 31 > Article 31 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols > Release on bail or personal surety is permissible for misdemeanors unless detention is required for operational integrity.

content.title: Article 32 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols
content.conditions: Release on bail is strictly prohibited in capital offenses, high treason, and desertion to the enemy.
content.formattedText: Article 32 > Article 32 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols > Release on bail is strictly prohibited in capital offenses, high treason, and desertion to the enemy.

content.title: Article 33 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols
content.conditions: Military detainees have the statutory right to family contact and confidential visits with their defense attorneys.
content.formattedText: Article 33 > Article 33 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols > Military detainees have the statutory right to family contact and confidential visits with their defense attorneys.

content.title: Article 34 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols
content.conditions: Periodic health examinations are conducted for military detainees to verify physical health and investigate abuse allegations.
content.formattedText: Article 34 > Article 34 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols > Periodic health examinations are conducted for military detainees to verify physical health and investigate abuse allegations.

content.title: Article 35 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols
content.conditions: A detained serviceman receives 50% pay while in custody, retroactively restored in full upon acquittal or dismissal of charges.
content.formattedText: Article 35 > Article 35 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols > A detained serviceman receives 50% pay while in custody, retroactively restored in full upon acquittal or dismissal of charges.

content.title: Article 36 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols
content.conditions: A combat field commander may detain an individual endangering unit safety for up to 72 hours before formal judicial arraignment.
content.formattedText: Article 36 > Article 36 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols > A combat field commander may detain an individual endangering unit safety for up to 72 hours before formal judicial arraignment.

content.title: Article 37 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols
content.conditions: Cadets of military academies under detention are remanded within academy quarters under the supervision of the college commandant.
content.formattedText: Article 37 > Article 37 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols > Cadets of military academies under detention are remanded within academy quarters under the supervision of the college commandant.

content.title: Article 38 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols
content.conditions: The detainee or defense counsel may appeal detention renewal orders before the competent military court within 3 days.
content.formattedText: Article 38 > Article 38 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols > The detainee or defense counsel may appeal detention renewal orders before the competent military court within 3 days.

content.title: Article 39 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols
content.conditions: The military prison commandant bears full legal responsibility for detainee safety and protection against degrading treatment.
content.formattedText: Article 39 > Article 39 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols > The military prison commandant bears full legal responsibility for detainee safety and protection against degrading treatment.

content.title: Article 40 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols
content.conditions: The detainee must be released immediately by judicial order if evidence is insufficient to sustain the charge.
content.formattedText: Article 40 > Article 40 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols > The detainee must be released immediately by judicial order if evidence is insufficient to sustain the charge.

content.title: Article 41 - Referral Authorities and Court Transmission
content.conditions: Referral powers reside in the Minister of Defense, Chief of Staff, and Division Commanders as prescribed by military directives.
content.formattedText: Article 41 > Article 41 - Referral Authorities and Court Transmission > Referral powers reside in the Minister of Defense, Chief of Staff, and Division Commanders as prescribed by military directives.

content.title: Article 42 - Referral Authorities and Court Transmission
content.conditions: A formal referral decision must set forth the defendant's identity, rank, unit, concise factual charge, penal statute, and trial venue.
content.formattedText: Article 42 > Article 42 - Referral Authorities and Court Transmission > A formal referral decision must set forth the defendant's identity, rank, unit, concise factual charge, penal statute, and trial venue.

content.title: Article 43 - Referral Authorities and Court Transmission
content.conditions: Minor infractions are referred by commanding officers to the Disciplinary Officer's Court for prompt summary adjudication.
content.formattedText: Article 43 > Article 43 - Referral Authorities and Court Transmission > Minor infractions are referred by commanding officers to the Disciplinary Officer's Court for prompt summary adjudication.

content.title: Article 44 - Referral Authorities and Court Transmission
content.conditions: Felonies and grave misdemeanors carrying custodial sentences are referred to the competent standing Military Court.
content.formattedText: Article 44 > Article 44 - Referral Authorities and Court Transmission > Felonies and grave misdemeanors carrying custodial sentences are referred to the competent standing Military Court.

content.title: Article 45 - Referral Authorities and Court Transmission
content.conditions: A Joint Military Court is formed by judicial decree where civilians and military personnel jointly commit offenses against armed forces security.
content.formattedText: Article 45 > Article 45 - Referral Authorities and Court Transmission > A Joint Military Court is formed by judicial decree where civilians and military personnel jointly commit offenses against armed forces security.

content.title: Article 46 - Referral Authorities and Court Transmission
content.conditions: The referral authority, upon prosecutorial recommendation, may file away proceedings if the act is non-criminal or the accused lacks capacity.
content.formattedText: Article 46 > Article 46 - Referral Authorities and Court Transmission > The referral authority, upon prosecutorial recommendation, may file away proceedings if the act is non-criminal or the accused lacks capacity.

content.title: Article 47 - Referral Authorities and Court Transmission
content.conditions: The referral authority may remand the file to investigators for supplemental inquiries prior to directing court referral.
content.formattedText: Article 47 > Article 47 - Referral Authorities and Court Transmission > The referral authority may remand the file to investigators for supplemental inquiries prior to directing court referral.

content.title: Article 48 - Referral Authorities and Court Transmission
content.conditions: Jurisdictional conflicts between civil criminal courts and military tribunals are resolved definitively by the Federal Court of Cassation.
content.formattedText: Article 48 > Article 48 - Referral Authorities and Court Transmission > Jurisdictional conflicts between civil criminal courts and military tribunals are resolved definitively by the Federal Court of Cassation.

content.title: Article 49 - Referral Authorities and Court Transmission
content.conditions: The Military Public Prosecutor may appeal dismissal or non-referral decisions to the Military Cassation Court within 30 days.
content.formattedText: Article 49 > Article 49 - Referral Authorities and Court Transmission > The Military Public Prosecutor may appeal dismissal or non-referral decisions to the Military Cassation Court within 30 days.

content.title: Article 50 - Referral Authorities and Court Transmission
content.conditions: Flag officers (Brigadier General and above) are tried before a military court presided over by an officer of equal or senior rank with career judges.
content.formattedText: Article 50 > Article 50 - Referral Authorities and Court Transmission > Flag officers (Brigadier General and above) are tried before a military court presided over by an officer of equal or senior rank with career judges.

content.title: Article 51 - Referral Authorities and Court Transmission
content.conditions: The referral order, witness list, and trial date must be served upon the accused and defense counsel at least 7 days before trial.
content.formattedText: Article 51 > Article 51 - Referral Authorities and Court Transmission > The referral order, witness list, and trial date must be served upon the accused and defense counsel at least 7 days before trial.

content.title: Article 52 - Referral Authorities and Court Transmission
content.conditions: The referral authority may amend the legal description of the charge based upon newly discovered facts and evidence.
content.formattedText: Article 52 > Article 52 - Referral Authorities and Court Transmission > The referral authority may amend the legal description of the charge based upon newly discovered facts and evidence.

content.title: Article 53 - Referral Authorities and Court Transmission
content.conditions: The relevant ministry is notified immediately upon an officer's referral to court to arrange administrative relief and interim command.
content.formattedText: Article 53 > Article 53 - Referral Authorities and Court Transmission > The relevant ministry is notified immediately upon an officer's referral to court to arrange administrative relief and interim command.

content.title: Article 54 - Referral Authorities and Court Transmission
content.conditions: Classified defense documents and operational plans are transmitted directly to the court president via secure diplomatic military courier.
content.formattedText: Article 54 > Article 54 - Referral Authorities and Court Transmission > Classified defense documents and operational plans are transmitted directly to the court president via secure diplomatic military courier.

content.title: Article 55 - Referral Authorities and Court Transmission
content.conditions: Promotion and annual increments are suspended from the date of the referral order until a final definitive judgment is rendered.
content.formattedText: Article 55 > Article 55 - Referral Authorities and Court Transmission > Promotion and annual increments are suspended from the date of the referral order until a final definitive judgment is rendered.

content.title: Article 56 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees
content.conditions: Hearings of military courts are public, unless the court decides to proceed in camera to safeguard operational defense secrets or order.
content.formattedText: Article 56 > Article 56 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees > Hearings of military courts are public, unless the court decides to proceed in camera to safeguard operational defense secrets or order.

content.title: Article 57 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees
content.conditions: The military court is constituted with a presiding officer and two military judges, attended by the military prosecutor and court clerk.
content.formattedText: Article 57 > Article 57 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees > The military court is constituted with a presiding officer and two military judges, attended by the military prosecutor and court clerk.

content.title: Article 58 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees
content.conditions: Presence of defense counsel is mandatory in all felony trials; the court appoints counsel at state defense expense if unrepresented.
content.formattedText: Article 58 > Article 58 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees > Presence of defense counsel is mandatory in all felony trials; the court appoints counsel at state defense expense if unrepresented.

content.title: Article 59 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees
content.conditions: Trial begins with the reading of the indictment and interrogating the defendant as to whether he pleads guilty or not guilty, without oath.
content.formattedText: Article 59 > Article 59 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees > Trial begins with the reading of the indictment and interrogating the defendant as to whether he pleads guilty or not guilty, without oath.

content.title: Article 60 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees
content.conditions: If the defendant makes a voluntary and unambiguous confession, the court may accept the plea and proceed to sentencing.
content.formattedText: Article 60 > Article 60 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees > If the defendant makes a voluntary and unambiguous confession, the court may accept the plea and proceed to sentencing.

content.title: Article 61 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees
content.conditions: The court examines prosecution witnesses, and the defendant and his counsel have the right to cross-examine each witness.
content.formattedText: Article 61 > Article 61 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees > The court examines prosecution witnesses, and the defendant and his counsel have the right to cross-examine each witness.

content.title: Article 62 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees
content.conditions: The court calls and examines defense witnesses requested by the accused or counsel, recording testimonies verbatim in court minutes.
content.formattedText: Article 62 > Article 62 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees > The court calls and examines defense witnesses requested by the accused or counsel, recording testimonies verbatim in court minutes.

content.title: Article 63 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees
content.conditions: The court may appoint ballistics, ordnance, and communications experts to present technical assessments on specialized military evidence.
content.formattedText: Article 63 > Article 63 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees > The court may appoint ballistics, ordnance, and communications experts to present technical assessments on specialized military evidence.

content.title: Article 64 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees
content.conditions: The accused shall always have the final statement, and defense counsel delivers the closing argument prior to closing deliberations.
content.formattedText: Article 64 > Article 64 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees > The accused shall always have the final statement, and defense counsel delivers the closing argument prior to closing deliberations.

content.title: Article 65 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees
content.conditions: Deliberations are conducted in absolute secrecy; judgments are adopted by majority vote, the president casting the deciding vote if tied.
content.formattedText: Article 65 > Article 65 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees > Deliberations are conducted in absolute secrecy; judgments are adopted by majority vote, the president casting the deciding vote if tied.

content.title: Article 66 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees
content.conditions: Sentences of capital punishment (death) require unanimous agreement of all tribunal members; lack of unanimity commutes to life imprisonment.
content.formattedText: Article 66 > Article 66 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees > Sentences of capital punishment (death) require unanimous agreement of all tribunal members; lack of unanimity commutes to life imprisonment.

content.title: Article 67 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees
content.conditions: Judgments are rendered in the Name of the People and read publicly in open court, stating findings of fact, statutory clauses, and penalties.
content.formattedText: Article 67 > Article 67 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees > Judgments are rendered in the Name of the People and read publicly in open court, stating findings of fact, statutory clauses, and penalties.

content.title: Article 68 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees
content.conditions: Judgments are entered into the military register and signed by the president, all panel members, and the court clerk immediately.
content.formattedText: Article 68 > Article 68 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees > Judgments are entered into the military register and signed by the president, all panel members, and the court clerk immediately.

content.title: Article 69 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees
content.conditions: The court explains to the convict his right to lodge a cassation appeal within thirty (30) days from judgment pronouncement.
content.formattedText: Article 69 > Article 69 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees > The court explains to the convict his right to lodge a cassation appeal within thirty (30) days from judgment pronouncement.

content.title: Article 70 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees
content.conditions: In-absentia trials proceed against fugitive personnel following public notice; in-absentia convictions fall upon arrest or surrender.
content.formattedText: Article 70 > Article 70 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees > In-absentia trials proceed against fugitive personnel following public notice; in-absentia convictions fall upon arrest or surrender.

content.title: Article 71 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees
content.conditions: Courtroom discipline and decorum are entrusted to the presiding judge, who may exclude disrupters and impose immediate summary contempt sanctions.
content.formattedText: Article 71 > Article 71 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees > Courtroom discipline and decorum are entrusted to the presiding judge, who may exclude disrupters and impose immediate summary contempt sanctions.

content.title: Article 72 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees
content.conditions: Court minutes recorded by the clerk reflect all procedures, evidence, motions, and pleas, enjoying authoritative evidentiary validity.
content.formattedText: Article 72 > Article 72 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees > Court minutes recorded by the clerk reflect all procedures, evidence, motions, and pleas, enjoying authoritative evidentiary validity.

content.title: Article 73 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees
content.conditions: If an offense is committed inside the courtroom during a session, the tribunal may summarily convict the offender or refer him for investigation.
content.formattedText: Article 73 > Article 73 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees > If an offense is committed inside the courtroom during a session, the tribunal may summarily convict the offender or refer him for investigation.

content.title: Article 74 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees
content.conditions: Witnesses and defense attorneys enjoy qualified judicial immunity for factual arguments and statements made in good faith in court.
content.formattedText: Article 74 > Article 74 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees > Witnesses and defense attorneys enjoy qualified judicial immunity for factual arguments and statements made in good faith in court.

content.title: Article 75 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees
content.conditions: Trial proceedings are stayed if the defendant is certified mentally incompetent to stand trial, ordering placement in a psychiatric hospital.
content.formattedText: Article 75 > Article 75 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees > Trial proceedings are stayed if the defendant is certified mentally incompetent to stand trial, ordering placement in a psychiatric hospital.

content.title: Article 76 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees
content.conditions: The military tribunal may adjudicate joined civil damage claims submitted by victims or state entities arising directly from the crime.
content.formattedText: Article 76 > Article 76 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees > The military tribunal may adjudicate joined civil damage claims submitted by victims or state entities arising directly from the crime.

content.title: Article 77 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees
content.conditions: The court orders restitution of seized properties to rightful owners in its final judgment, unless subject to statutory confiscation.
content.formattedText: Article 77 > Article 77 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees > The court orders restitution of seized properties to rightful owners in its final judgment, unless subject to statutory confiscation.

content.title: Article 78 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees
content.conditions: The tribunal, upon finding substantiated judicial mitigating grounds, may commute death to life imprisonment or reduce custodial penalties.
content.formattedText: Article 78 > Article 78 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees > The tribunal, upon finding substantiated judicial mitigating grounds, may commute death to life imprisonment or reduce custodial penalties.

content.title: Article 79 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees
content.conditions: The court enters a verdict of acquittal if innocence is proven, or dismisses for insufficient evidence, interpreting all doubts in favor of the accused.
content.formattedText: Article 79 > Article 79 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees > The court enters a verdict of acquittal if innocence is proven, or dismisses for insufficient evidence, interpreting all doubts in favor of the accused.

content.title: Article 80 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees
content.conditions: Case files involving death or life imprisonment are automatically transmitted to the Military Cassation Court for mandatory review without appeal.
content.formattedText: Article 80 > Article 80 - Trial Sessions, Evidence, and Defense Guarantees > Case files involving death or life imprisonment are automatically transmitted to the Military Cassation Court for mandatory review without appeal.

content.title: Article 81 - Appellate Review and Military Court of Cassation
content.conditions: The Military Court of Cassation headquartered in Baghdad is established, composed of senior military judges to review military appeals.
content.formattedText: Article 81 > Article 81 - Appellate Review and Military Court of Cassation > The Military Court of Cassation headquartered in Baghdad is established, composed of senior military judges to review military appeals.

content.title: Article 82 - Appellate Review and Military Court of Cassation
content.conditions: The time limit for filing a cassation appeal is thirty (30) days, commencing the day following in-person pronouncement or service of default judgment.
content.formattedText: Article 82 > Article 82 - Appellate Review and Military Court of Cassation > The time limit for filing a cassation appeal is thirty (30) days, commencing the day following in-person pronouncement or service of default judgment.

content.title: Article 83 - Appellate Review and Military Court of Cassation
content.conditions: Grounds of cassation appeal include breach of statutory law, erroneous application or interpretation, essential procedural defect, or defective reasoning.
content.formattedText: Article 83 > Article 83 - Appellate Review and Military Court of Cassation > Grounds of cassation appeal include breach of statutory law, erroneous application or interpretation, essential procedural defect, or defective reasoning.

content.title: Article 84 - Appellate Review and Military Court of Cassation
content.conditions: The Military Cassation Court may affirm the verdict, quash it and remand for retrial, or reduce the sentence in accordance with law.
content.formattedText: Article 84 > Article 84 - Appellate Review and Military Court of Cassation > The Military Cassation Court may affirm the verdict, quash it and remand for retrial, or reduce the sentence in accordance with law.

content.title: Article 85 - Appellate Review and Military Court of Cassation
content.conditions: The Military Cassation Court cannot aggravate the penalty if the appeal was lodged solely by the convict without cross-appeal by the prosecution.
content.formattedText: Article 85 > Article 85 - Appellate Review and Military Court of Cassation > The Military Cassation Court cannot aggravate the penalty if the appeal was lodged solely by the convict without cross-appeal by the prosecution.

content.title: Article 86 - Appellate Review and Military Court of Cassation
content.conditions: The convict or the prosecution may petition for rectification of a cassation decision within 30 days based on grave substantive error of law.
content.formattedText: Article 86 > Article 86 - Appellate Review and Military Court of Cassation > The convict or the prosecution may petition for rectification of a cassation decision within 30 days based on grave substantive error of law.

content.title: Article 87 - Appellate Review and Military Court of Cassation
content.conditions: Retrial (motion for reconsideration) of final convictions may be petitioned if newly discovered evidence conclusively establishes innocence.
content.formattedText: Article 87 > Article 87 - Appellate Review and Military Court of Cassation > Retrial (motion for reconsideration) of final convictions may be petitioned if newly discovered evidence conclusively establishes innocence.

content.title: Article 88 - Appellate Review and Military Court of Cassation
content.conditions: Interlocutory procedural orders rendered during trial cannot be appealed independently from the final judgment disposing of the action.
content.formattedText: Article 88 > Article 88 - Appellate Review and Military Court of Cassation > Interlocutory procedural orders rendered during trial cannot be appealed independently from the final judgment disposing of the action.

content.title: Article 89 - Appellate Review and Military Court of Cassation
content.conditions: The En Banc Full Bench of the Military Cassation Court adjudicates capital executions, landmark legal controversies, and trials of general officers.
content.formattedText: Article 89 > Article 89 - Appellate Review and Military Court of Cassation > The En Banc Full Bench of the Military Cassation Court adjudicates capital executions, landmark legal controversies, and trials of general officers.

content.title: Article 90 - Appellate Review and Military Court of Cassation
content.conditions: The Chief Military Cassation Prosecutor presents a reasoned written brief on every dossier reviewing legality and recommending disposition.
content.formattedText: Article 90 > Article 90 - Appellate Review and Military Court of Cassation > The Chief Military Cassation Prosecutor presents a reasoned written brief on every dossier reviewing legality and recommending disposition.

content.title: Article 91 - Appellate Review and Military Court of Cassation
content.conditions: Decisions of the Military Court of Cassation rendered within its jurisdiction are definitive, res judicata, and immediately enforceable.
content.formattedText: Article 91 > Article 91 - Appellate Review and Military Court of Cassation > Decisions of the Military Court of Cassation rendered within its jurisdiction are definitive, res judicata, and immediately enforceable.

content.title: Article 92 - Appellate Review and Military Court of Cassation
content.conditions: If a judgment is quashed and remanded a second time, the trial court must conform strictly to the directives of the Cassation Court.
content.formattedText: Article 92 > Article 92 - Appellate Review and Military Court of Cassation > If a judgment is quashed and remanded a second time, the trial court must conform strictly to the directives of the Cassation Court.

content.title: Article 93 - Appellate Review and Military Court of Cassation
content.conditions: A cassation appeal automatically stays the execution of capital sentences and custodial penalties until final determination.
content.formattedText: Article 93 > Article 93 - Appellate Review and Military Court of Cassation > A cassation appeal automatically stays the execution of capital sentences and custodial penalties until final determination.

content.title: Article 94 - Appellate Review and Military Court of Cassation
content.conditions: Appeals may be formally lodged through the military garrison prison warden or unit commander, who must transmit it to court within 24 hours.
content.formattedText: Article 94 > Article 94 - Appellate Review and Military Court of Cassation > Appeals may be formally lodged through the military garrison prison warden or unit commander, who must transmit it to court within 24 hours.

content.title: Article 95 - Appellate Review and Military Court of Cassation
content.conditions: Military convicts and detained servicemen are fully exempt from judicial court fees for cassation appeals and retrial petitions.
content.formattedText: Article 95 > Article 95 - Appellate Review and Military Court of Cassation > Military convicts and detained servicemen are fully exempt from judicial court fees for cassation appeals and retrial petitions.

content.title: Article 96 - Enforcement of Sentences and Final Provisions
content.conditions: Sentences of capital punishment (death) cannot be executed until ratified by presidential decree issued by the President of the Republic.
content.formattedText: Article 96 > Article 96 - Enforcement of Sentences and Final Provisions > Sentences of capital punishment (death) cannot be executed until ratified by presidential decree issued by the President of the Republic.

content.title: Article 97 - Enforcement of Sentences and Final Provisions
content.conditions: Execution is carried out by firing squad in a garrison or military prison, attended by the judge, prosecutor, physician, and clergy.
content.formattedText: Article 97 > Article 97 - Enforcement of Sentences and Final Provisions > Execution is carried out by firing squad in a garrison or military prison, attended by the judge, prosecutor, physician, and clergy.

content.title: Article 98 - Enforcement of Sentences and Final Provisions
content.conditions: Execution of capital punishment is strictly barred on official national holidays and religious feast days of the convict's faith.
content.formattedText: Article 98 > Article 98 - Enforcement of Sentences and Final Provisions > Execution of capital punishment is strictly barred on official national holidays and religious feast days of the convict's faith.

content.title: Article 99 - Enforcement of Sentences and Final Provisions
content.conditions: Execution of a pregnant female service member is deferred until childbirth and the completion of two years of nursing.
content.formattedText: Article 99 > Article 99 - Enforcement of Sentences and Final Provisions > Execution of a pregnant female service member is deferred until childbirth and the completion of two years of nursing.

content.title: Article 100 - Enforcement of Sentences and Final Provisions
content.conditions: Sentences of confinement are executed within military prisons under the administrative supervision and inspection of military magistrates.
content.formattedText: Article 100 > Article 100 - Enforcement of Sentences and Final Provisions > Sentences of confinement are executed within military prisons under the administrative supervision and inspection of military magistrates.

content.title: Article 101 - Enforcement of Sentences and Final Provisions
content.conditions: General amnesty extinguishes military convictions; executive pardon remits or commutes penalties without removing disciplinary stigmas.
content.formattedText: Article 101 > Article 101 - Enforcement of Sentences and Final Provisions > General amnesty extinguishes military convictions; executive pardon remits or commutes penalties without removing disciplinary stigmas.

content.title: Article 102 - Enforcement of Sentences and Final Provisions
content.conditions: The military prisoner is discharged immediately upon expiration of his term upon written certification from prison authorities.
content.formattedText: Article 102 > Article 102 - Enforcement of Sentences and Final Provisions > The military prisoner is discharged immediately upon expiration of his term upon written certification from prison authorities.

content.title: Article 103 - Enforcement of Sentences and Final Provisions
content.conditions: Military Criminal Procedure Code No. 30 of 2007 is hereby repealed and superseded by this Code.
content.formattedText: Article 103 > Article 103 - Enforcement of Sentences and Final Provisions > Military Criminal Procedure Code No. 30 of 2007 is hereby repealed and superseded by this Code.

content.title: Article 104 - Enforcement of Sentences and Final Provisions
content.conditions: The Minister of Defense in concurrence with the Chief of Military Justice shall promulgate implementing regulations.
content.formattedText: Article 104 > Article 104 - Enforcement of Sentences and Final Provisions > The Minister of Defense in concurrence with the Chief of Military Justice shall promulgate implementing regulations.

content.title: Article 105 - Enforcement of Sentences and Final Provisions
content.conditions: Judgments and judicial actions taken prior to the entry into force of this Code remain valid unless quashed on appeal.
content.formattedText: Article 105 > Article 105 - Enforcement of Sentences and Final Provisions > Judgments and judicial actions taken prior to the entry into force of this Code remain valid unless quashed on appeal.

content.title: Article 106 - Enforcement of Sentences and Final Provisions
content.conditions: Staffing establishments of military tribunals, cassation benches, and prosecution offices are organized under Cabinet regulations.
content.formattedText: Article 106 > Article 106 - Enforcement of Sentences and Final Provisions > Staffing establishments of military tribunals, cassation benches, and prosecution offices are organized under Cabinet regulations.

content.title: Article 107 - Enforcement of Sentences and Final Provisions
content.conditions: All state ministries, intelligence agencies, and armed units must facilitate the military judiciary's mission and execute its mandates.
content.formattedText: Article 107 > Article 107 - Enforcement of Sentences and Final Provisions > All state ministries, intelligence agencies, and armed units must facilitate the military judiciary's mission and execute its mandates.

content.title: Article 108 - Enforcement of Sentences and Final Provisions
content.conditions: This Code shall enter into force from the date of its publication in the Iraqi Official Gazette (Al-Waqaei Al-Iraqiya) No. 4444 on April 24, 2017.
content.formattedText: Article 108 > Article 108 - Enforcement of Sentences and Final Provisions > This Code shall enter into force from the date of its publication in the Iraqi Official Gazette (Al-Waqaei Al-Iraqiya) No. 4444 on April 24, 2017.

content.title: Definitions and Scope of Regulation
content.conditions: This Regulation is promulgated to execute the provisions of Peshmerga Service and Retirement Law No. 38 of 2007, governing administrative affairs, promotion rosters, medical commissions, and service calculation.
content.formattedText: Article 1 > Definitions and Scope of Regulation > This Regulation is promulgated to execute the provisions of Peshmerga Service and Retirement Law No. 38 of 2007, governing administrative affairs, promotion rosters, medical commissions, and service calculation.

content.title: Service Verification and Auditing Boards
content.conditions: Central and sub-committees are constituted within the Ministry of Peshmerga to audit and authenticate personnel records and struggle service rendered prior to March 5, 1991.
content.formattedText: Article 2 > Service Verification and Auditing Boards > Central and sub-committees are constituted within the Ministry of Peshmerga to audit and authenticate personnel records and struggle service rendered prior to March 5, 1991.

content.title: Officer Promotion Protocols and Rosters
content.conditions: Officer promotions are tabulated semiannually (Nowruz roster on March 21 and Army Day roster on January 6) upon fulfilling statutory time in rank, completing mandatory courses, and positive command evaluations.
content.formattedText: Article 3 > Officer Promotion Protocols and Rosters > Officer promotions are tabulated semiannually (Nowruz roster on March 21 and Army Day roster on January 6) upon fulfilling statutory time in rank, completing mandatory courses, and positive command evaluations.

content.title: Enlistment Regulations and Military Discipline
content.conditions: All Peshmerga units adhere to regular military disciplinary standards, with mandatory periodic medical examinations evaluating physical fitness for operational deployment.
content.formattedText: Article 4 > Enlistment Regulations and Military Discipline > All Peshmerga units adhere to regular military disciplinary standards, with mandatory periodic medical examinations evaluating physical fitness for operational deployment.

content.title: Pension Processing and Severance Gratuity Workflow
content.conditions: The General Directorate of Peshmerga Pension Affairs finalizes retirement dossiers pursuant to Article 28 calculations and disburses end-of-service gratuities under Article 29 via the Ministry of Finance.
content.formattedText: Article 5 > Pension Processing and Severance Gratuity Workflow > The General Directorate of Peshmerga Pension Affairs finalizes retirement dossiers pursuant to Article 28 calculations and disburses end-of-service gratuities under Article 29 via the Ministry of Finance.

content.title: Effective Date
content.conditions: This Regulation shall be enforced from the date of issuance and published in the Official Gazette (Waqaei Kurdistan).
content.formattedText: Article 6 > Effective Date > This Regulation shall be enforced from the date of issuance and published in the Official Gazette (Waqaei Kurdistan).

content.title: Unification and Audit of Peshmerga Payroll and Establishment
content.conditions:
First: Unification of all accounting units of Peshmerga forces within the official statutory framework of the Ministry of Peshmerga and Ministry of Finance.
Second: Comprehensive audit of Peshmerga personnel files to cleanse payrolls from duplicate or illicit entitlements.
Third: Mandatory electronic biometric verification linking salary payments to unique personal numbers (UPN).
Fourth: Re-audit of disability pension beneficiary rosters under Law No. 34 of 2007, canceling any unlawful entitlements.
content.formattedText:
Article 4 > Unification and Audit of Peshmerga Payroll and Establishment > First: Unification of all accounting units of Peshmerga forces within the official statutory framework of the Ministry of Peshmerga and Ministry of Finance.
Second: Comprehensive audit of Peshmerga personnel files to cleanse payrolls from duplicate or illicit entitlements.
Third: Mandatory electronic biometric verification linking salary payments to unique personal numbers (UPN).
Fourth: Re-audit of disability pension beneficiary rosters under Law No. 34 of 2007, canceling any unlawful entitlements.

content.title: Regularization and Audit of Counted Revolutionary Service
content.conditions: Re-verification and documentary auditing of all credited revolutionary struggle years pursuant to official archival proof and requirements under Laws No. 33 and 38 of 2007.
content.formattedText: Article 6 > Regularization and Audit of Counted Revolutionary Service > Re-verification and documentary auditing of all credited revolutionary struggle years pursuant to official archival proof and requirements under Laws No. 33 and 38 of 2007.

content.title: Harmonization of Military Pensions Under 2007 Statutes
content.conditions: Strict enforcement of Laws No. 33, 34, and 38 of 2007 regarding military retirement, invalidating fictitious ranks or allowances granted contrary to statutory procedures.
content.formattedText: Article 9 > Harmonization of Military Pensions Under 2007 Statutes > Strict enforcement of Laws No. 33, 34, and 38 of 2007 regarding military retirement, invalidating fictitious ranks or allowances granted contrary to statutory procedures.

content.title: Prohibition of Unlawful Dual Emoluments
content.conditions: Strict prohibition against receiving multiple salaries or unauthorized allowances from the public treasury, requiring beneficiaries to rectify status within statutory deadlines.
content.formattedText: Article 10 > Prohibition of Unlawful Dual Emoluments > Strict prohibition against receiving multiple salaries or unauthorized allowances from the public treasury, requiring beneficiaries to rectify status within statutory deadlines.

content.title: Legal Accountability and Penal Liability
content.conditions: Any official or officer intentionally furnishing fraudulent records or enabling illicit disbursements shall be prosecuted before competent courts, with full restitution under government debt recovery statutes.
content.formattedText: Article 16 > Legal Accountability and Penal Liability > Any official or officer intentionally furnishing fraudulent records or enabling illicit disbursements shall be prosecuted before competent courts, with full restitution under government debt recovery statutes.

content.title: Amendment of Article 1 (Coverage of Reservists and Duty Crimes)
content.conditions: Clause (a) of Paragraph (First) is amended and Clause (e) added to Article 1 so that the code applies to active Armed Forces personnel for crimes committed during or resulting from service, and to active reservist officers and soldiers.
content.formattedText: Article 1 > Amendment of Article 1 (Coverage of Reservists and Duty Crimes) > Clause (a) of Paragraph (First) is amended and Clause (e) added to Article 1 so that the code applies to active Armed Forces personnel for crimes committed during or resulting from service, and to active reservist officers and soldiers.

content.title: Amendment of Article 7 (Definitions of Military Mutiny and Room Detention)
content.conditions: Adds two new clauses to Article 7: Sixth: Military Mutiny: Refusal to obey lawful superior orders, violent resistance, or unlawful assembly to abstain from military duty; Seventh: Room Detention: Confinement of personnel to a dedicated quarter within camp bounds.
content.formattedText: Article 2 > Amendment of Article 7 (Definitions of Military Mutiny and Room Detention) > Adds two new clauses to Article 7: Sixth: Military Mutiny: Refusal to obey lawful superior orders, violent resistance, or unlawful assembly to abstain from military duty; Seventh: Room Detention: Confinement of personnel to a dedicated quarter within camp bounds.

content.title: Amendment of Article 10 (Original Penalties Structure)
content.conditions: Amends execution protocols of capital punishment by firing squad, ensuring judicial guarantees and harmonizing life and temporary imprisonment provisions.
content.formattedText: Article 3 > Amendment of Article 10 (Original Penalties Structure) > Amends execution protocols of capital punishment by firing squad, ensuring judicial guarantees and harmonizing life and temporary imprisonment provisions.

content.title: Amendment of Article 15 (Mandatory and Discretionary Expulsion)
content.conditions: Mandatory expulsion or contract annulment applies upon convictions of capital punishment, imprisonment, terrorism, or dishonorable crimes; discretionary upon simple confinement sentences; mandatory dismissal of officers losing commissioning criteria.
content.formattedText: Article 4 > Amendment of Article 15 (Mandatory and Discretionary Expulsion) > Mandatory expulsion or contract annulment applies upon convictions of capital punishment, imprisonment, terrorism, or dishonorable crimes; discretionary upon simple confinement sentences; mandatory dismissal of officers losing commissioning criteria.

content.title: Enforcement of First Amendment
content.conditions: This amendment enters into force upon publication in Iraqi Official Gazette No. 4238 on May 7, 2012.
content.formattedText: Article 5 > Enforcement of First Amendment > This amendment enters into force upon publication in Iraqi Official Gazette No. 4238 on May 7, 2012.
